questions.explain: The chapter's triage key: TSQL steps port almost anywhere, while SSIS, CmdExec, and PowerShell steps each need platform-specific rebuilds.
options: SSIS
PowerShell
TSQL
CmdExec
questions.q: When inventorying Agent jobs for cloud migration, which step-subsystem column value in msdb indicates steps that port almost anywhere?

questions.explain: Azure SQL Database has no SQL Server Agent; the native replacement is elastic jobs — a job service backed by a job database that executes T-SQL across databases, even better than Agent at multi-database targeting, but limited to T-SQL.
options: Azure Automation only
Elastic jobs, which execute T-SQL across one or many databases on a schedule
SQL Server Agent installed on a VM
Always On availability groups
questions.q: What is the native replacement for SQL Server Agent on Azure SQL Database?

questions.explain: Agent jobs live in msdb on each instance and are not replicated to the secondary in a failover group. The chapter's pattern is to deploy identical jobs to both instances and gate execution to run only on the primary.
options: To enable automatic job replication to the secondary
Because jobs in msdb are not replicated to the secondary, so without a primary-only gate jobs would run twice or not at all after failover
Because Managed Instance has no Agent
To pause jobs during geo-replication seeding
questions.q: On a Managed Instance in a failover group, why must scheduled Agent jobs check sys.dm_hadr_database_replica_states for the PRIMARY role?

questions.explain: RDS includes SQL Server Agent, but there is no OS to touch — no CmdExec or PowerShell steps touching the OS, no file system access, no xp_cmdshell. Those jobs must be reimplemented with platform services.
options: T-SQL maintenance jobs
Job schedules and alerts
CmdExec or PowerShell steps that touch the OS
Database Mail notifications
questions.q: On RDS for SQL Server, which Agent job capability is explicitly restricted?

questions.explain: The chapter's sequence ends with keeping the on-premises Agent running in parallel until the cloud automation has executed successfully on its own schedule at least twice.
options: All jobs must be converted to elastic jobs
The cloud automation must have executed successfully on its own schedule at least twice — 'it ran once' is not proven
All SSIS packages must be deleted
The msdb database must be shrunk below 100 MB
questions.q: Per the chapter's migration sequence, what must be true before the on-premises Agent can be retired?
